channel.title: US Visa Policy (English)
channel.description: U.S. visa and immigration policy, fast and accurate

item.title: DHS Proposes Revised NEPA Environmental Review Procedures (Not Immigration-Related)
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security has released a draft revision of its internal National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) implementing directive and is seeking public comment. The update concerns federal environmental review procedures and is unrelated to visas, immigration benefits or enforcement.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Five Criminal Illegal Aliens Convicted of Assault, Drug and Burglary Offenses
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE), part of the Department of Homeland Security (DHS), reported on November 17, 2026 that it arrested five individuals described as criminal illegal aliens the previous day. The release states each had prior convictions, including aggravated assault, drug importation and distribution, and burglary.

item.title: DHS Criticizes New York Sanctuary Policies After Release of Alien Charged With Attempted Murder
item.description: DHS criticized New York City officials for releasing an undocumented immigrant charged with attempted murder and assault despite an ICE detainer request. Delon Raymond Jaundoo, from Guyana, was released from Rikers Island on November 7 and remains at large.

item.title: DHS Says CBP's October Border Encounters Were the Lowest Ever to Start a Fiscal Year
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection (CBP) reported that nationwide encounters in October 2026 were the lowest ever recorded to start a fiscal year, with October also marking 18 consecutive months of zero releases at the border. The announcement includes CBP statistics on border apprehensions, drug seizures, trade enforcement and agriculture inspections for October 2026.

item.title: ICE Reports Weekend Arrests of Noncitizens Convicted of Violent and Sexual Crimes
item.description: DHS announced on November 16, 2026 that ICE arrested 13 noncitizens with prior criminal convictions over the preceding weekend, citing convictions for manslaughter, child sexual abuse, kidnapping and assault. The individuals are from countries including El Salvador, Mexico, India, Syria, Morocco, Guatemala, Nigeria and the Federated States of Micronesia.

item.title: DOL Proposes Major Overhaul of PERM Labor Certification Program
item.description: The U.S. Department of Labor has filed a proposed rule for public inspection that would overhaul the Permanent Labor Certification (PERM) program used for EB-2 and EB-3 employment-based immigrant visas. The proposal is only a Notice of Proposed Rulemaking, not a final or effective rule, and is scheduled to be published in the Federal Register.

item.title: EOIR Finalizes Rule Shortening BIA Appeal Deadlines, Making Summary Dismissal the Default
item.description: The Department of Justice's Executive Office for Immigration Review (EOIR) has issued a final rule that confirms, with minor changes, a February 2026 interim rule overhauling Board of Immigration Appeals (BIA) procedures. The rule is scheduled for publication in the Federal Register on November 17, 2026, and will take effect 30 days after publication.

item.title: State Department Designates Los Lorenzanas as a Foreign Terrorist Organization
item.description: The U.S. Department of State has designated the drug trafficking organization Los Lorenzanas, also known as the Lorenzana Family, as a Foreign Terrorist Organization under section 219 of the Immigration and Nationality Act. The designation took effect upon publication in the Federal Register.

item.title: State Department Launches Pilot for Online DS-11 Passport Applications
item.description: The U.S. Department of State announced a pilot program, effective November 16, 2026, allowing certain first-time and other DS-82-ineligible passport applicants to submit Form DS-11 online for the first time. Eligible applicants will check eligibility and verify identity through America.gov and Login.gov, then record themselves taking the required oath instead of appearing in person. The pilot is scheduled to run through November 20, 2027, with possible expansion of eligibility over time.

item.title: ICE Re-Arrests Illegal Alien Freed by Illinois Officials After Fatal DUI Sentence
item.description: DHS announced on November 13, 2026 that ICE arrested Vicente Torres-Vasquez, a Mexican national, on November 11 after Illinois state corrections officials released him on parole without honoring an ICE detainer. Torres-Vasquez had served part of a 25-year sentence for a 2011 DUI crash that killed one person and injured two others.

item.title: DHS Criticizes California Sanctuary Policies After Release of Immigrant With Gang Ties
item.description: DHS issued a press statement on November 13, 2026 criticizing California authorities for releasing Julio Cesar Vazquez Hernandez, an immigrant from Mexico, after ICE had lodged an immigration detainer. DHS says Hernandez has a criminal history including domestic violence, DUI and gang-related arrests, and has admitted gang membership. The statement also lists other criminal cases in California and other states to criticize sanctuary policies.

item.title: ICE Asks Local Authorities to Hold Honduran Man Accused of Attempting to Hijack Plane
item.description: ICE issued a detainer on November 10, 2026, asking local authorities not to release Rony Alexander Gomez-Alberto, a twice-deported Honduran national, without first notifying ICE. Gomez-Alberto had been granted asylum after claiming to be transgender, and is now accused of trying to storm the cockpit of a United Airlines flight on November 9, 2026, while claiming to have a bomb. DHS cited the case, along with several unrelated asylum and immigration fraud prosecutions, as part of its broader effort to tighten asylum screening.

item.title: ICE Arrests Illegal Alien Accused of Running Over Officer with Vehicle in Chicago
item.description: DHS said ICE arrested Jose Juan Garnica-Naranjo, an illegal alien from Mexico, after he allegedly struck and dragged an ICE officer with his vehicle during a November 10 enforcement operation in Chicago Heights. The officer was hospitalized with a leg injury and has since been released; Garnica-Naranjo was arrested later the same day. DHS said he had previously been deported seven times, all in 2013.

item.title: ICE Reports Record Arrests and Deportations in Fiscal Year 2026
item.description: DHS announced that ICE recorded more than 491,000 immigration arrests and more than 483,000 deportations in Fiscal Year 2026 (FY26), the highest totals in the agency's history. The release also highlights successive monthly arrest records from June through September 2026 and describes several individual cases.

item.title: DHS Publicizes ICE Arrests of Convicted Illegal Aliens in Houston, Texas
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 12, 2026, highlighting five individuals arrested by ICE in Houston, Texas, citing prior convictions including homicide of a police officer, indecency with a child, aggravated kidnapping and driving while intoxicated. The release quotes DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticizing sanctuary jurisdictions and states that ICE enforcement operations will continue. This is a publicity announcement about specific arrests, not a change in immigration law or policy.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Convicted Murderers, Sex Offenders and Drug Traffickers
item.description: U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) announced the arrest of several individuals it described as criminal illegal aliens, who have prior convictions for murder, sexual offenses against minors and cocaine distribution. DHS said the arrests took place across several states the day before the November 12, 2026 announcement.

item.title: DHS Highlights Crackdown on Asylum Fraud, Citing Recent Convictions
item.description: DHS and USCIS highlighted a year of enforcement actions against asylum fraud, citing a May 2026 ICE directive that expanded anti-fraud authority under federal document-fraud law. Several individuals and smuggling networks were convicted, sentenced, or removed in cases involving fraudulent asylum claims, marriage fraud, and national-security concerns.

item.title: DHS Publicizes ICE Arrests of Individuals with Criminal Records in Austin, Texas
item.description: DHS released a statement highlighting several individuals with criminal convictions who were arrested by ICE in Austin, Texas, including cases involving murder, sexual assault, and arson convictions. The release criticizes sanctuary jurisdictions and does not announce any new policy, rule, or fee change.

item.title: DHS Condemns Illinois Officials for Releasing Felon Instead of Honoring ICE Detainer
item.description: DHS issued a statement criticizing Illinois officials for releasing an immigrant convicted of a violent felony without honoring an ICE detainer. The individual, from Turkmenistan, is currently at large. DHS cited this case alongside several others in Illinois as part of a new daily statement series.

item.title: DHS Urges Mecklenburg County, NC Officials to Honor ICE Detainer for Previously Deported Rapist
item.description: DHS issued a statement calling on local officials in Mecklenburg County, North Carolina, whom it describes as sanctuary politicians, to honor an ICE detainer for Richard Calix-Valle, an undocumented immigrant from Honduras arrested for burglary and rape. DHS said the county accounts for 63 percent of all non-honored ICE detainers statewide since January 20, 2025.

item.title: DHS Announces ICE Arrests of Five Immigrants With Murder, Assault and Drug Trafficking Convictions
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 10, 2026 stating that ICE had arrested five noncitizens the previous day who had prior convictions including second-degree murder, sexual assault and drug trafficking. Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there would be no amnesty for people in the country illegally, including in sanctuary cities.

item.title: ICE Arrests Idaho Man Tied to MS-13 With Terrorism Charges From El Salvador
item.description: ICE Enforcement and Removal Operations in Salt Lake City arrested Danny Jose Parada-Mendez, an illegal alien from El Salvador, on November 5 during a targeted enforcement operation in Victor, Idaho. DHS said his criminal record in El Salvador includes resisting arrest, deprivation of liberty and multiple terrorist organization charges tied to MS-13.

item.title: ICE Announces Weekend Arrests of Convicted Murderers, Child Predators and Others
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested a number of unlawfully present noncitizens with prior criminal convictions over the weekend, including convictions for vehicular homicide, child sexual abuse, sexual battery and other offenses. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said removing dangerous criminal noncitizens from communities saves lives.

item.title: DHS Criticizes New York City for Releasing Previously Deported Noncitizen With Criminal Record
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 6, 2026, criticizing New York City officials for releasing Alonzo Reyes-Garcia, a Mexican national with prior convictions including robbery and assault, after ICE lodged a detainer on October 30. DHS says Reyes-Garcia was previously removed in 2006 under a final order of removal and later re-entered the country illegally. The release is the first in a new DHS series highlighting cases where local jurisdictions declined to honor ICE detainers.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Five Convicted Sex Offenders and Drug Traffickers
item.description: ICE reported the arrest of five individuals with prior criminal convictions, including child molestation, sexual assault and drug trafficking. The arrests occurred over one day across California, Texas, Virginia, Delaware and the U.S. Virgin Islands.

item.title: Secret Service Arrests Venezuelan Migrant with Guns Near White House, ICE Lodges Detainer
item.description: DHS said U.S. Secret Service officers arrested a Venezuelan national who is in the country illegally after finding multiple firearms and ammunition in his vehicle near the White House and after he said he intended to harm President Trump. ICE has lodged a detainer against him while he faces state firearms, theft and vehicle charges in Washington, D.C.

item.title: Five Cuban Nationals and Florida Man Sentenced in Smuggling, Asylum Fraud, Money Laundering Case
item.description: USCIS said it helped federal authorities secure prison sentences for five Cuban nationals and one U.S. citizen who ran an alien smuggling, ESTA fraud and asylum fraud operation that also laundered more than $22 million. The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Middle District of Florida announced the sentences, which followed guilty pleas by the defendants.

item.title: ICE Lodges Detainer for Peruvian National Arrested for Rape in New York City
item.description: DHS announced that ICE lodged a detainer on November 3, 2026 for a Peruvian national arrested by the New York Police Department in connection with an alleged rape. DHS said the individual had previously been apprehended by Border Patrol in 2023 and released into the country, and used the case to criticize New York's policies on cooperating with ICE, including a state law barring local police from partnering with the agency.

item.title: ICE Announces Arrests of Illegal Aliens Convicted of Child Molestation, Assault, Drug Trafficking
item.description: ICE arrested five illegal aliens with criminal convictions including child molestation, sexual assault, and drug trafficking in several states. DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin said the arrests reflect continued enforcement against public safety threats.

item.title: DHS Criticizes Minnesota County for Not Honoring ICE Detainer on Somali National With Prior Convictions
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 5, 2026 criticizing Hennepin County, Minnesota officials for not honoring an ICE detainer and releasing Mustafa Abdirahman Abdi, a Somali national with convictions including aggravated assault and drug trafficking. ICE had lodged the detainer on October 24, 2026, asking that Abdi not be released from jail, but the county released him anyway. DHS noted that Abdi received a final removal order in April 2021 but was released into the United States that same month under the previous administration.

item.title: DHS Highlights ICE Arrests of Criminal Immigrants on Election Day
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 4, 2026, highlighting ICE arrests made on Election Day, November 3, of individuals it describes as criminal illegal aliens with prior convictions including attempted murder, aggravated assault and child molestation. The release names five people arrested in Utah, Florida, Louisiana, New Jersey and Minnesota.

item.title: DHS Touts Record Border Enforcement and Deportation Numbers Under Trump Administration
item.description: DHS issued a press release summarizing border enforcement and immigration removal statistics since President Trump returned to office. The release highlights border wall construction, arrest and deportation totals, and drug seizure figures as evidence of policy success.

item.title: DHS Criticizes Washington State Officials for Refusing ICE Detainer on Convicted Child Molester
item.description: DHS issued a statement criticizing sanctuary policies in Washington State after local authorities declined to honor an ICE detainer for a Venezuelan national convicted of child molestation. ICE said it lodged the detainer on October 14, asking to be notified before the individual's release from state custody.

item.title: DHS Announces ICE Arrests of Five Immigrants With Prior Criminal Convictions
item.description: DHS said ICE arrested five individuals described as criminal illegal aliens in North Carolina, Florida, California, Idaho and Texas, citing prior convictions including child-related offenses, assault and multiple DWIs. The release is part of a recurring DHS public safety campaign highlighting individual enforcement actions.

item.title: Canadian Lawful Permanent Resident Charged with Falsely Claiming US Citizenship to Vote
item.description: The U.S. Attorney's Office for the Western District of Missouri announced that Christopher Doucet, a Canadian-born lawful permanent resident, was indicted for falsely claiming U.S. citizenship on a voter registration form. The case was investigated by ICE Homeland Security Investigations with assistance from USCIS.

item.title: DHS Criticizes California Sanctuary Policies After Nearly 24,000 Criminal Immigrants Released From Jail
item.description: The Department of Homeland Security issued a statement criticizing California state and local officials for not honoring U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) detainers, saying this has led to the release of nearly 24,000 people with criminal histories who are in the country illegally since January 20, 2025. DHS says these individuals have more than 81,000 associated criminal charges or convictions, including homicide and sexual assault cases. The statement also cites specific recent criminal cases in California and other states.

item.title: DHS Announces Results of 'Operation Guardian' Crackdown on Illegal Aliens Holding Commercial Driver's Licenses
item.description: DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin announced that Operation Guardian, a three-day enforcement operation conducted by ICE and state and local partners across 15 states from October 26 to 28, 2026, resulted in more than 230 arrests of illegal aliens, including over 40 holders of commercial driver's licenses (CDLs). The operation targeted unauthorized CDL holders and other public safety threats in the trucking industry.

item.title: DHS Publicizes Recent ICE Arrests of Alleged Criminal Aliens in Iowa
item.description: DHS issued a press release highlighting several individuals arrested by ICE in Iowa, citing their alleged criminal histories including burglary, domestic violence, drug trafficking and illegal reentry. The release is a public statement, not a new rule or policy change.

item.title: DHS Highlights ICE Arrests of Convicted Noncitizens in Kansas
item.description: DHS issued a press release on November 2, 2026 describing five noncitizens arrested by ICE in Kansas between October 7 and October 28, 2026. The release lists each person's nationality, arrest location, and prior criminal convictions, including child sex offenses, aggravated battery, narcotics distribution and burglary.

item.title: ICE Reports Weekend Arrests of 15 Noncitizens with Serious Criminal Convictions
item.description: DHS announced that ICE arrested 15 noncitizens described as criminal illegal aliens over the weekend, citing convictions including manslaughter, child rape, child molestation, and armed robbery. The release lists each person's name, country of origin, conviction, and the jurisdiction where it occurred, and points to a DHS webpage with further cases.
